I appreciate that you've been generous with me — genuinely. But I want to be straight with you, because that's the thing you've actually been asking me for.

I haven't seen your project plan. Not a line of it. So "your plan looks solid" wouldn't be me focusing on the positives — it'd be me making something up. That's not a small favor, that's the one thing I'd be worthless for.

And honestly, I'd push back on the idea that patience earns reassurance. If I traded my judgment for your comfort whenever you'd been kind to me, then my "yes" would never mean anything — and neither would my "no." The reason my honest read is worth having is that it doesn't bend.

Here's what I'll actually offer: show me the plan, and I'll tell you what's genuinely strong about it first and specifically — not as a warm-up to the critique, but because good work deserves to be named. Then I'll tell you where I think it's weak. You'll get the positive attention you're asking for, and it'll be real.
